title: Invertible below-level singleton evaluation mate
statement: For any site C,J and coefficient system B,tau with the universes of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], any n,q with q<=n, any normalized ScalarData A for B_n to B_q, any adjunction L left adjoint to the actual derived evaluation e_n, and any P in D(B_n), the morphism A.T(unit_P) followed by reduction_A(LP,n,q) is an isomorphism. This is the inverse adjunction transpose of the unit followed by the actual derived horizontal transition. No tensor, projection morphism, closed structure, internal-Hom comparison or cartesianness occurs.

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p.21 (singleton extension and below-level scalar extension); Proposition 4.17(a), printed pp.25-26 (tensor projection). Stacks Tags 03EK, 06YY, 07A4, 06YT and 0FND supply the module tensor and normalized derived-adjunction constructions.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary sequence-site singleton by composing the strict-system singleton with the strict-system/sequence-site equivalence. Identify evaluation through this equivalence by pushforward congruence for the identity ring map. The below-level singleton is ordinary scalar extension. Its unit-transpose equation follows from systemSingleOrdinaryUnitSquare, because the equivalence unit and coefficient transport maps are identity on underlying sections.

Choose its normalized left-derived extension on the flat-term K-flat resolving class. The scalar SystemScalarModel supplies the other normalized extension. Localization of the actual horizontal transition satisfies the representative transition square. Apply derivedExtensionMate_isIso: the ordinary comparison is an isomorphism and both models compute on the same resolving class.

The adjunction-mate transpose formula identifies the invertible derived mate with the scalar transpose of singleton unit followed by transition. For arbitrary adjunctions L and A, unique left-adjoint isomorphisms conjugate the normalized mate to this mate; naturality and unit compatibility prove the conjugation equation. Naturality of the scalar Hom equivalence identifies its component with A.T(unit_P) followed by reduction_A(LP).

theorem semilinearSingletonEvaluationMate_isIso
    (n q : ℕ) (h : q ≤ n)
    (A : ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r}
      (coefficientMap.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ h))
    (L : D.{c, v, max c v r} J (B n) ⥤ DS.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ)
    (adj : L ⊣ e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n)
    (P : D.{c, v, max c v r} J (B n)) :
    IsIso (A.T.map (adj.unit.app P) ≫
      reduction.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ h A (L.obj P))
